component.name: Wayfinder Aura
component.summary: Voice dictation that types for you

description.p: Wayfinder Aura is a local-first voice dictation and speech recognition application for Linux. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words are typed wherever your cursor is: in X11 and XWayland apps, and in native Wayland apps on KDE Plasma through the desktop's remote-control portal (the desktop asks once; GNOME 45+ is expected to work but is not yet verified). No cloud required: by default, speech-to-text transcription runs offline on your device with whisper.cpp — in local mode your voice never leaves your computer. Optional cloud transcription backends are available if you choose to enable them, and the app checks online for model updates (this can be turned off in config.json).

Free tier includes Base/Base.en transcription on CPU, local minimal cleanup, hotkeys, text injection, the status overlay, and audio-processing controls. Wayfinder Aura Ultra is an optional one-time purchase ($29.99 until 31 December 2026, then $60 from 1 January 2027) that unlocks GPU acceleration, additional speech and cleanup models, styles and voice profiles, custom vocabulary, chunked long-form recording, and optional cloud backends. Ultra is sold on wayfindercollective.io (not through Flathub billing); enter a license key in Settings after purchase.

ul.li: Local-first & Private — transcribed on your device by default; optional cloud backends if you choose them
Hotkey Triggered — Press a key to start/stop recording
Wayland & X11 Support — X11 and XWayland apps directly; native Wayland apps on KDE Plasma through the desktop's remote-control portal (GNOME 45+ not yet verified)
System Tray Integration — Runs quietly in the background
Base Dictation — Free local CPU transcription with optional minimal cleanup
Ultra Acceleration — GPU inference, additional models, styles, and long-form chunking
Configurable Typing Speed — Instant paste or simulated typing

description.p: Perfect for writing emails, documents, code comments, chat messages, or any situation where speaking is faster than typing.

description.p: Faster local dictation, dependable sandbox integration, and clearer update behavior:

ul.li: Local cleanup models can stay loaded between dictations, substantially reducing repeated cleanup latency while retaining a save-memory option
Flatpak hotkeys use the desktop's GlobalShortcuts portal, show the compositor's live bindings, and open the desktop shortcut editor instead of presenting settings that cannot take effect
Downloaded speech and cleanup models are verified against pinned fingerprints, size-bounded, and kept on secure connections across redirects
CPU-versus-GPU benchmarks warm models first, separate one-time loading from processing, and retire stale results when a model is unavailable
Installed users are notified when a newer applicable GitHub release is available, while Flathub installs follow Flathub's managed update channel
Flatpak audio feedback is isolated from microphone capture teardown for more reliable repeated dictation

description.p: Portable HTTPS and startup reliability across Linux distributions:

ul.li: Model downloads, license activation, and catalog requests now use a bundled current CA trust store on Bazzite, Fedora, SteamOS, and other distributions
TLS certificate verification remains fully enabled and is exercised from the finished AppImage and installed Flatpak before release
AppImage runtime extraction uses the private disk-backed user cache instead of relying on limited RAM-backed /tmp space

description.p: Reliable microphone capture in distributed Linux packages:

ul.li: AppImage dictation records through the host PipeWire graph instead of opening raw ALSA devices that can return silence or wedge on Bazzite and SteamOS
Flatpak capture uses its pinned Pulse/PipeWire sandbox boundary
AppImage and Flatpak builds now block release unless their real packaged microphone helpers receive audio frames
Manual microphone selections and Auto-detect mode remain stable across device refreshes and restarts

description.p: Reliable packaged behavior on Bazzite, SteamOS, and modern Linux desktops:

ul.li: Fixed silent AppImage mic-test playback caused by bundled ALSA libraries conflicting with the host PipeWire stack
Free and CPU-only modes now run independently linked CPU inference binaries without initializing Vulkan
Free-tier restrictions are enforced in the interface, saved configuration, and runtime backends; Free uses Base transcription on CPU
Benchmarks always show Base transcription speed and compare CPU with an explicitly labeled Ultra GPU preview where supported
Light, Medium, and Heavy audio processing now have distinct, package-tested behavior and clearer guidance
One-shot transcription is the accuracy-first default; optional Ultra chunking uses a tested 15-second/2-second-overlap profile
Steam Deck setup and back-button guidance are rootless, hardware-aware, and work with Desktop and Game Mode
Fixed text rendering roughly twice as large as intended on HiDPI (150–200%) desktops; the interface now looks identical on every display
The interface typeface now ships with the app instead of depending on what each distribution substitutes — the same build looks the same everywhere
Fixed the status overlay getting stuck mid-screen on KDE, and the placement and position controls that did nothing with it
Fixed system tools (typing service setup, browser links, microphone listing) being launched with the app's bundled libraries on newer distributions
UI scale buttons now step 25% per click, so large adjustments take a couple of clicks instead of a dozen
The AppImage now adds itself to your applications menu on first launch (icon included), and follows the file if you move it
Every release is now boot-tested before publishing, with GPU, typing, and packaging integrity gates

description.p: Major reliability release — install-and-it-works on modern Linux desktops:

ul.li: Fixed startup crash on newer distributions (GLib 2.88, e.g. Fedora 44 / Bazzite)
Typing now sets itself up: one-click background typing service, no terminal needed
Typing works reliably across desktops, with honest error reporting when it can't
First-run setup no longer attempts system package installs on immutable distros
The best installed speech model is selected automatically
Always On overlay now works in packaged builds, with polished rendering
New defaults: Ctrl+Alt+Space to dictate; optional auto-Enter after dictation
Background-noise annotations are no longer typed into your text
GPU detection fixed for recent AMD graphics cards
Flatpak builds now include GPU (Vulkan) dictation
